question: Which of the following actions will create a new folder on a Windows desktop?

options.text: Right-clicking on the desktop and selecting 'New' → 'Folder
Clicking on the Recycle Bin icon

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Right-clicking on the desktop and selecting 'New' → 'Folder'**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Creating a new folder on a Windows desktop can be easily achieved by** right-clicking on the desktop space**.
 
• After right-clicking, a** context menu** appears with several options such as 'View', 'Sort by', 'Refresh', 'New', etc.
 
• Select the 'New' option, which opens a secondary menu with options to create different items like** Folder, Shortcut, Text Document, etc.**
 
• Clicking on 'Folder' creates a** new folder** on the desktop, which appears with the default name 'New Folder'.
 
• The user can** rename the folder** immediately by typing the desired name or later by right-clicking on the folder and selecting 'Rename'.
 
• This method is a** graphical user interface (GUI)-based approach**, making it simple and intuitive for users of all skill levels.
 
• The process works on** most Windows operating systems**, including Windows 7, 8, 10, and 11.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alt + Tab**__

 __
 
• Alt + Tab is a keyboard shortcut used to **switch between open applications or windows** on a computer.
 
• This shortcut does not relate to creating folders but enhances** multitasking efficiency**.
 
 
 
• **Recycle Bin Icon**__
 __
 
• Clicking on the **Recycle Bin icon** allows users to **view deleted files** and restore or permanently delete them.
 
• The Recycle Bin is part of Windows' **file management system**, but it cannot be used to create folders.
 
 
 
• **Ctrl + F**__
 
 
• Ctrl + F is a shortcut used to** find text or specific items** within a document, webpage, or application.
 
• It is commonly used for** searching content** but has no function related to creating folders.
